perturbation_or_case: Severe acquired brain injury; no observable command following at bedside
evidence_quality: large prospective cohort (n=353; relevant no-command subgroup n=241)
language: not uniformly established; verbal instructions used
agency: internal command following demonstrated in subset
motor_report: absent observable command following by inclusion
what_survives: ability to follow some commands covertly in 25% of behaviorally nonresponsive subgroup
interpretation_limit: Covert command following is evidence of preserved cognitive processing but does not by itself exhaust phenomenal consciousness

perturbation_or_case: Extensive bilateral lesions involving insula, ACC, mPFC and medial temporal structures
interoception: insula damage; detailed interoceptive consequence not core endpoint
what_survives: core self-recognition; agency; stable self-concept; much introspective self-awareness
interpretation_limit: One case falsifies simple necessity claims more readily than it establishes a positive distributed mechanism
reference: Philippi et al. PLOS ONE 2012 DOI:10.1371/journal.pone.0038413

method: lesion cohort with perception and memory metacognition tasks
vision: objective perceptual performance comparable to controls
memory: objective memory task and memory metacognition relatively preserved
conscious_content: visual task content available enough for objective performance
interpretation_limit: Shows a dissociation of performance and metacognitive access; does not localize self or consciousness

method: pre/post lesion bodily-self and heartbeat-awareness experiment
self_location: cardio-visual manipulation produced abnormal bodily-self effects including bi-location
conscious_content: conscious bodily experience altered rather than abolished
what_survives: general wakeful subjectivity and task participation
interpretation_limit: Demonstrates a bodily-self component can be perturbed without equating insula with the whole subject

perturbation_or_case: Primary visual cortex lesions with hemianopic field defects
vision: normal conscious vision lost in affected field; some patients retained crude conscious motion-like experience
conscious_content: selective visual contents altered/absent in lesioned field; residual conscious vision possible
what_survives: nonvisual subjectivity and in some cases residual visual awareness
what_drops: normal visual awareness for affected field
interpretation_limit: Selective sensory loss is not loss of the subject; residual pathways/plasticity complicate necessity claims
reference: Alexander & Cowey et al. Brain 2011 PMID:21097490

method: simultaneous thalamic/cortical recordings and causal DBS
vision: sensory processing measured but not human report
agency: arousal behavior restored by specific stimulation
wakefulness: wake-like state restored from anesthesia by location/frequency-specific CL stimulation
interpretation_limit: Strong evidence for thalamocortical control of conscious state/arousal in macaque; not evidence that thalamus alone is consciousness

perturbation_or_case: Low-intensity focused ultrasound to distinct thalamic regions during near-threshold vision
vision: ventroanterior thalamic modulation changed object-recognition sensitivity
interpretation_limit: Modulating access threshold is not equivalent to creating or abolishing consciousness

perturbation_or_case: Focal epilepsy with post-ictal language testing after recorded seizures
evidence_quality: clinical cohort; detailed speech analysis available in 46 patients
language: post-ictal aphasia in 20/46 adequately analyzable patients; multiple deficit types
motor_report: speech/language report impaired in affected episodes
conscious_content: language content/report selectively disrupted in subgroup
what_survives: other behavior can remain sufficient for clinical interaction/testing
interpretation_limit: Post-ictal aphasia is heterogeneous and cannot identify the mechanism of any one person's transient episode
reference: Ferri et al. Brain and Language 2026 DOI:10.1016/j.bandl.2026.105766

perturbation_or_case: Skilled abacus user after right-hemisphere stroke involving dorsal premotor and inferior parietal regions
language: available; linguistic calculation strategy could compensate during impairment
vision: visual imagery-based mental-abacus strategy impaired; ordinary vision not reported abolished
memory: mental-abacus digit memory selectively impaired while basic arithmetic knowledge survived
self_recognition: preserved enough for longitudinal self-report and testing
agency: general agency and physical abacus operation preserved
motor_report: available; physical abacus could still be operated
what_survives: basic arithmetic facts; knowledge and operation of physical abacus; later recovery of visuospatial mental-abacus strategy
what_drops: mental-abacus calculation and digit-memory strategy transiently lost
interpretation_limit: Single case supports selective loss of a learned internal strategy/tool more strongly than any general theory of internal simulation or self
reference: Tanaka et al. Frontiers in Psychology 2012 DOI:10.3389/fpsyg.2012.00315
